title: Collect the sprites for the release
prompt:
The 1.0 release needs every sprite from Mira’s `art` folder.

1. Create the folder `release/1.0/sprites` in Mira’s home directory, with all the folders on the way, in one command.
2. Copy every `.png` file from `art` into it, and nothing else.
hints: `mkdir` creates missing parent folders with the option `-p`.
The glob `*.png` matches every name ending in `.png`.
`cp art/*.png release/1.0/sprites/` copies all of them at once.
check:
d=release/1.0/sprites
if [ -d $d ]; then ok "~/$d exists."; else no "There is no folder ~/$d yet."; exit 1; fi
n=$(ls $d | grep -c '\.png$')
if [ "$n" = 7 ]; then ok "It holds all 7 PNG sprites."; else no "It holds $n PNG files; art has 7."; fi
other=$(ls $d | grep -vc '\.png$')
if [ "$other" = 0 ]; then ok "It holds nothing but PNG files."; else no "It holds $other file(s) that aren’t PNG sprites."; fi

title: Only the single-digit bosses
prompt: In `art` there are three boss sprites: `boss1.png`, `boss2.png` and `boss10.png`. Move only `boss1.png` and `boss2.png` into `art/backup`, with one `mv` command that uses a glob, so that `boss10.png` stays where it is.
hints: `*` matches any number of characters, so `boss*.png` would catch `boss10.png` too.
check:
if [ -f art/backup/boss1.png ] && [ -f art/backup/boss2.png ]; then ok "boss1.png and boss2.png are in art/backup."; else no "boss1.png and boss2.png aren’t both in art/backup."; fi
if [ ! -e art/boss1.png ] && [ ! -e art/boss2.png ]; then ok "They are gone from art: moved, not copied."; else no "art still has boss1.png or boss2.png. Move them, don’t copy them."; fi
if [ -f art/boss10.png ] && [ ! -e art/backup/boss10.png ]; then ok "boss10.png stayed in art."; else no "boss10.png should stay in art."; fi

title: Notes and notes
prompt:
The `art` folder has two notes files whose names differ only in case: `notes.txt` and `Notes.txt`. On Linux they are two separate files.

Rename the capitalised one, `Notes.txt`, to `notes-old.txt` in the same folder. Leave `notes.txt` as it is. Look at both with `cat` first.
hints: Linux file names are case-sensitive: `notes.txt` and `Notes.txt` are different names.
`mv` renames a file when the target is a new name in the same folder.
check:
if [ "$(cat art/notes-old.txt 2> /dev/null)" = 'Capitalised notes' ]; then ok "art/notes-old.txt holds the capitalised notes."; else no "art/notes-old.txt doesn’t hold the contents of Notes.txt."; fi
if [ ! -e art/Notes.txt ]; then ok "art/Notes.txt is gone."; else no "art/Notes.txt is still there."; fi
if [ "$(cat art/notes.txt 2> /dev/null)" = 'lower-case notes' ]; then ok "art/notes.txt is unchanged."; else no "art/notes.txt changed or is gone; it should stay as it was."; fi
